extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and research-integrity practitioners/readers of Retraction Watch
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying, scoring, and retracting articles produced or manipulated by paper mills (especially within special issues), and the publisher-level processes, checks, and communications needed to do that at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancies in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Hindawi as an indicator of manipulation — e.g., articles that are outside the scope of the special issue or journal may signal papermill submissions. Example from commenters: whole special-issue articles that do not match topic or journal scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancies in the description of the research reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies in the description of the research reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mismatch between stated aims/methods/results and what is actually described can indicate inauthentic or fabricated work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancies between the availability of data and the research described
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies between the availability of data and the research described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about data that are unsupported by available datasets or incompatible with described methods are treated as a red flag for manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation patterns (irrelevant, self-serving, or otherwise inappropriate references) are considered an indicator of publication manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incoherent, meaningless, and/or irrelevant content
rubrics_metrics.description: Incoherent, meaningless, and/or irrelevant content included in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text that is nonsensical, filler, or irrelevant to the stated topic is a hallmark of papermill-produced manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compromised or manipulated peer-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Compromised or manipulated peer-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that the peer-review process was falsified or otherwise corrupted (e.g., fake reviewers, fabricated reports) is grounds for retraction because it undermines trust in the publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive checklist of papermill hallmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a comprehensive checklist of specific hallmarks of papermill papers to reassess manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi halted special issues and reassessed manuscripts 'with a comprehensive checklist of specific hallmarks of papermill papers.' This checklist is the basis for triage and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-and-threshold retraction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Score articles according to checklist criteria and retract all articles that meet a defined threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi 'created a checklist of criteria for scoring articles, and all that met a certain threshold were retracted.' This enables rapid, large-scale action but requires defined scoring and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual trained human assessment and questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two trained evaluators assess each paper and complete a structured questionnaire in bespoke software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi outsourced assessments, trained evaluators, and required that at least two people evaluate each paper to reduce individual bias and provide reproducible adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computational tools to detect fabricated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational tools provide supporting evidence about fabricated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated analyses can flag likely fabrication in text, figures, or data; used to supplement human review rather than replace it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computational tools to detect plagiarized peer-review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational tools used to detect plagiarized peer-review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated comparison/forensics can reveal copied or recycled reviewer reports indicating peer-review manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computational tools to flag suspect peer-review turnaround times
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational tools used to flag suspect peer-review turn-around times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely rapid or patterned turnaround times may indicate manipulated or fake review processes and should trigger further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating independent sleuths' findings (PubPeer and lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect, evaluate, and categorize comments provided on PubPeer and compile independent sleuths’ lists as part of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi built on work by independent researchers (e.g., Smut Clyde list) and used PubPeer comments as additional intelligence to prioritize investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized, limited-detail retraction notices for scale and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized wording for retraction notices and intentionally limit specific details of what is under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi limited details to avoid sharing intelligence with bad actors and to communicate with thousands of authors rapidly. Trade-off: less transparency for external researchers versus operational security and speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halt and reassess special-issue publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Halt publication of special issues and reassess all special issue manuscripts when manipulation is suspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary suspension of special issues allows comprehensive reassessment using the checklist and prevents further infiltration while systems are strengthened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen checks on editors, authors, and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out thorough review and strengthening of existing checks on editors, authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes vetting identities/credentials, monitoring behavior, and enforcing stricter requirements for those roles; resulted in bans for implicated guest editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter vetting of special-issue proposals and guest editors (scrutinize topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute much more stringent checks on proposals for special issues and on guest editors; scrutinize proposed topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts note that verifying identities alone is insufficient; topics that are catch-all or duplicative invite papermill submissions and deserve additional scrutiny before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banning implicated editors and authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Ban guest editors and authors associated with paper mills from future editorial roles and publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi banned 'several hundred' guest editors as a remedial step; recommendation includes sharing information about banned individuals with other publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue expressions of concern for entire special issues when warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue expressions of concern for entire special issues to alert readers when multiple papers are suspected but not yet investigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to warn readers to exercise caution in interpreting papers in suspect issues while investigations continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction rationale: publication process undermined
rubrics_metrics.description: Retract when evidence shows the publication process has been undermined and the publisher can no longer vouch for the article's integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hindawi frames retraction decisions on whether manipulation/evidence indicates the integrity of the publication process is compromised, not necessarily on naming all specific defects in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational recommendations: fund, credit, and cooperate with independent sleuths
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund independent sleuths, credit their work, and cooperate with them in investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External experts recommended that publishers financially support and acknowledge pro-bono investigators and aggregate their findings to improve detection and remediation.
